# gomes-open-weight-paradox-2026
- **URL:** https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17413 (PDF: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.17413; submitted 19 Apr 2026; 23 pp.) · **Accessed:** 2026-09-16 · **For:** v1 response round, compute-governance predecessor / co-option risk
- **What it establishes:** A 2026 single-author paper that (a) names the co-option risk of hardware-layer controls, (b) cites Sastry et al. 2024 verbatim for the "double-edged sword" point, and (c) proposes four institutional safeguards: multilateral/quorum authorization, tamper-evident transparency logs, sunset clauses, and formal civil-society seats with audit access. Full title: "The Open-Weight Paradox: Why Restricting Access to AI Models May Undermine the Safety It Seeks to Protect." Printed page = PDF page.
- **Key passages:**
  - Sec. VII "Limits and Objections," p. 17: "Hardware-level controls could be co-opted for purposes unrelated to AI safety: surveillance of legitimate research activity, suppression of commercial competitors, or politically motivated denial of computing access. The concern is not hypothetical."
  - p. 17 (citing Vipra 2024): "the function creep characteristic of surveillance technologies makes this trajectory likely rather than speculative."
  - p. 17: "First, activation of enforcement mechanisms … should require multilateral authorization rather than unilateral decision." "Second, every governance action … should be recorded in tamper-evident transparency logs subject to independent audit. Third, governance mandates should incorporate sunset clauses requiring periodic re-authorization … Fourth, civil society organizations should hold formal seats in the oversight architecture".
  - Sec. VIII "Conclusion," rec. (5), p. 19: "explicit civil liberties safeguards, including multilateral quorum requirements for activating constraints, transparency logs of all governance actions, independent civil society audits, and sunset clauses requiring periodic re-authorization, to prevent the co-option of chip-level controls for censorship or political repression".
  - Abstract: "with explicit safeguards against the co-option of hardware controls for domestic repression."
- **Reliability:** Primary, but a non-peer-reviewed preprint by a single author (Vinicius Santana Gomes, "Special Advisor, Government of the Federal District of Brazil; AI Instructor, School of Government of the Federal District of Brazil"). Advocacy-leaning (pro-openness, Global South framing). Useful as evidence the co-option/safeguards framing is now in the literature; not authoritative on its own.
- **Relevance to this project:** Second predecessor for the essay's governance test; shows the "who can flip the switch / logs / sunset / audit" questions are already articulated. Reference: Vinicius Santana Gomes, "The Open-Weight Paradox: Why Restricting Access to AI Models May Undermine the Safety It Seeks to Protect," arXiv:2604.17413 (Apr. 2026).
